vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: hugging-face-cli
Version: 1.0.2

The skill provides a comprehensive interface for the official Hugging Face CLI ('hf'), enabling repository management, dataset interaction, and cloud job execution. It includes explicit safety rules requiring user confirmation for destructive actions and provides clear instructions for secure token handling. While it suggests a 'curl | bash' installation method in the documentation, this points to the official Hugging Face domain (hf.co) and is standard practice for this tool.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose (wrapping the official hf CLI) and only requests the HF_TOKEN and the hf binary, but pay attention to installer instructions and token scope because the skill can perform destructive write actions.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (Hugging Face CLI) matches what it requires and instructs: it needs the hf CLI binary and an HF_TOKEN. The commands listed (upload, delete, deploy, jobs, endpoints, etc.) align with the Hugging Face Hub functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the Hub management scope (listing, uploading, downloading, creating/deleting repos, running jobs, managing endpoints, cache management). It instructs handling local files when uploading/syncing and to set HF_TOKEN via environment variable. Note: the doc explicitly recommends avoiding interactive 'hf auth login', and gives broad examples including destructive commands (repo/bucket/endpoint deletion). There is no instruction to read unrelated system files or other secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry install spec is a Homebrew formula 'hf' (reasonable). However SKILL.md includes alternate installation commands that pipe remote install scripts to the shell (curl https://hf.co/cli/install.sh | bash and PowerShell one-liners). Those installer lines are common for CLI tools but are higher-risk (download-and-execute). The skill itself does not automatically download code; the installer guidance is manual.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only HF_TOKEN is required/configured as the primary credential, which is appropriate. The SKILL.md explains the difference between read and write tokens; write-level tokens are needed for destructive actions (create/delete/upload/deploy). No unrelated credentials or extra environment variables are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable. It does not request permanent system-level presence or to modify other skills' configs. Autonomous invocation is enabled by default (normal) but not an additional flagged privilege here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is a wrapper for the official Hugging Face CLI and is internally consistent, but take these precautions before installing or using it:
- Only provide the minimum HF_TOKEN scope you need: prefer a Read token for downloads and inspections; only use a Write token if you must upload/delete/deploy.
- The registry lists Homebrew as the install method (safer); if you use the curl|bash installer shown in SKILL.md, inspect the install script first — piping remote scripts to the shell is higher-risk.
- Be aware many example commands are destructive (repos, buckets, endpoints, delete operations). Confirm any delete/upload actions explicitly and avoid letting automated agents run destructive commands without your approval.
- If you plan to let an autonomous agent use this skill, restrict the agent's permissions or avoid giving it a Write-scoped HF_TOKEN. If you want stronger safety, keep the skill user-invocable only and do not allow background/autonomous runs.
- No other credentials are requested, and the skill does not ask to read unrelated system files, but always review command output and actions before proceeding.
